feed.title: Agent N's Hermes News - Social Summaries
feed.subtitle: Daily social category summaries

entry.title: Social Summary: September 25, 2026
entry.summary:
Official Hermes Agent updates — The clear #1 story is @NousResearch's announcement that web search in Hermes Agent is now fast and free, powered by Perplexity AI's Fast Search. @Teknium also confirmed that Wizards are open-source coded, and ran a cluster of practical support replies confirming macOS/Windows/Linux cross-platform compatibility, with a follow-up confirming macOS support specifically, and directing users to the plugin directory. Sentiment here is enthusiastic and engaged — users are actively probing platform support and capabilities.

Oh-My-Hermes (OMH) plugin ecosystem — @rlaope generated the loudest third-party momentum: an all-in-one OMH plugin showcase (coding intelligence, subagent auto-routing, long-term memory), six new Jev Skills (omh-jev-ask, route, failure-triage, review-gate, action-check, done-check) adding typed, probability-based decision-making to Hermes workflows, and a hype-style claim of 50B tokens spent enhancing the Hermes Agent Runtime. Reaction is energetic but promotional in tone; several bare OMH link-drops were excluded as low-value.

Industry news (adjacent to Hermes) — Sakana AI's announcement of Jürgen Schmidhuber as Chief Scientific Advisor drew the batch's strongest engagement. @hardmaru added valuable context, linking Schmidhuber's pioneering 1990s work on meta-learning, recursive self-improvement, and world models to the Darwin Gödel Machine, The AI Scientist, and Sakana's Tokyo RSI Lab.

Community — @Teknium's Bangkok event promo performed well (120 likes, ~13.7k views), and high-goodwill posts (16k views on an appreciation post) reflect a warm, engaged audience. A heated @rlaope–@noxleeminho reply chain (tone disputes, JEV pricing) contained no product content and was excluded from the ranking, as were redundant/low-context replies.

entry.title: Social Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
Bot Screen / Live Desktop Passthrough launch (lead story): The week belonged to Hermes Desktop — @NousResearch announced Bot Screen real-time streaming of any agent's session (419k views, 2,048 likes) and @Teknium followed with the interactive desktop passthrough for Hermes Agent (176k views), letting users visually watch and take over the same machine their agent works on. An official @tonbistudio walkthrough with docs (559 likes) rounded out the launch, amplified by @Teknium; lead-dev reactions like "Finallllly!" and "Much needed!" (205 likes) signaled the feature was long-awaited and landed with strong excitement.

oh-my-hermes ecosystem: @rlaope had a productive week, open-sourcing jeval for Jev evaluation/visualization and shipping a major oh-my-hermes (OMH) update adding Jev skills and model routing (aliases, plugins, workflow routing, fast decision-making), positioning OMH as the all-in-one plugin for hermes-agent users — grassroots momentum despite modest engagement.

Tips & maintainer presence: @NousResearch shared a practical tip to use Hermes via iMessage with any model of choice. @Teknium stayed highly visible in the threads: correcting an attribution error (the work "is by us," not Anthropic), disputing a cache-bug report while directing users to file reproducible issues, and confirming a quick fix for community-reported feedback. Sentiment is celebratory around the launch and appreciative of responsive maintainer support; one contrarian community take praised Claude Opus 5.5 (GA 2026-09-22) while staying skeptical of Claude Code. Low-substance emoji replies and link drops were deprioritized.
